report.answer_text:
Gold rose about 60–65% in 2025. Spot gold started the year near $2,600 an ounce and ended around $4,300–$4,330. Sources differ on the exact percentage.
Fox Business reports gold surged 66% in 2025, the best gain since 1979.[1] It says gold sat at $2,606 last December and settled around $4,325 at year-end.[1]
Investing.com says it surged more than 60%, its strongest annual performance in decades.[2]
A late-December report put the gain at 72.8%, but that was measured at the Dec. 26 peak near $4,527, before gold slipped back by year-end.
One source cites 44%, which is likely a different measure, such as an average-price comparison. Another cites only 18–20%, which doesn't fit the price data, so I'd disregard it.
Records set:
Best year in decades: Most sources call it gold's biggest annual gain since 1979. A few say 1980.
Dozens of all-time highs: Metals Focus counted 56 fresh record highs.[3] FXStreet says gold set over 50 record peaks.[4]
Price milestones:
In April, gold briefly broke through $3,500.[5]
On Sept. 30 it reached a quarterly high of $3,858.41.[5]
It hit an all-time high of $4,379.13 on Oct. 17.[5]
It reached a record $4,527 an ounce on Dec. 26.[6]
Other records: Global gold mine production rose to a record 3,817 tonnes.[3] Silver also had a record year, with a gain of more than 142%.[1]
Drivers: Analysts cited central bank buying, safe-haven demand amid geopolitical uncertainty, a weaker US dollar, and Federal Reserve rate cuts.
